findings.description: SWR-TIM-001 and SWR-TIM-002 require detection no later than 100 µs after the limit expires. The element schedules decisive event B at limit + 100 µs, then allows a further 100 µs of handler latency, permitting detection 200 µs after expiry.
findings.requested_change: Specify a detection mechanism and latency bound that meet the 100 µs deadline while preserving the equality rule.

findings.description: The element says a start or completion event cancels pending compare events and event B raises nothing if the task has since started or completed. A start or completion after the configured limit but before event B is processed can therefore escape detection, despite SWR-TIM-001 through SWR-TIM-004.
findings.requested_change: Define how the stored event instants are compared with the limits and how a late start or completion is reported even if it occurs before the compare handler runs.

findings.description: The description says a detection count returns to zero only after 60 seconds of fault-free operation and never at power-on, but later says power-on clears the counts. SWR-LAT-009 requires the counts to be cleared at power-on.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the contradictory power-on behavior and specify clearing the detection counts as required by SWR-LAT-009.

findings.description: SWR-DIA-001 requires each applicable fault report within 10 ms. This interface explicitly allows later reports in a larger burst to miss that deadline; OP-SWC-009 defers the burst limit to verification, which cannot establish the missing architecture-level guarantee.
findings.requested_change: Provide a supported transmission and admission design that meets the deadline for all required reports, or raise a blocking decision on the conflicting burst and timing requirements.

findings.description: The cycle-end compare is required to occur within each 10 ms cycle after the execution-limit expiry of every released task, including T_DIAG. CON-SUP-103 gives T_DIAG a 20 ms execution limit, so its expiry cannot precede the end of its release cycle.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the cycle-end scheduling and supervision interaction against the configured T_DIAG limit and the end-of-cycle flow-check requirement.

findings.description: The start-up task cites OP-SWC-001 for execution time but states no task stack or other memory budget, and that open point addresses execution budgets rather than memory.
findings.requested_change: Allocate a justified memory budget to the start-up task or record the missing budget as an open point.

findings.description: The control-cycle task cites OP-SWC-001 for execution time but states no task stack or other memory budget, and that open point addresses execution budgets rather than memory.
findings.requested_change: Allocate a justified memory budget to the control-cycle task or record the missing budget as an open point.
